instruction: Launch a Chrome tab with the web link from the first message in the Bills email folder.

metadata.explanation: Variation 5: Uses 'launch' verb for opening action. Task requires launching a new Chrome tab with the first link (https://www.amazon.com/) from the Bills folder's latest email. Evaluator confirms the presence of all three URLs in Chrome tabs.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator cannot verify the instruction was actually followed - it only checks the end result (URLs open), not the process
No verification that the link came from the Bills email folder or from any email at all
No verification that Thunderbird was accessed or that the first message was read
Critical false positive vulnerability: agent could simply type/open amazon.com directly without reading any email and pass evaluation
Expected URLs include pre-opened tabs (apple.com, scholar.google.com) from config, evaluator cannot distinguish which tab was opened by completing the task
The evaluator checks presence of three URLs but cannot verify causality - that amazon.com was opened BECAUSE it was extracted from the email
Incomplete coverage: instruction requires email interaction but evaluator only checks Chrome tabs state
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add getter to verify Thunderbird Bills folder was accessed and first message was read (e.g., check accessibility tree for Thunderbird window state)
Add getter to extract the actual URL from the first message in Bills folder and verify it matches the opened tab
Consider using multi-step evaluator: (1) verify email was opened, (2) verify correct link was extracted, (3) verify link was opened in Chrome
Alternative: Use a Chrome history getter to verify the amazon.com tab was opened AFTER Thunderbird interaction (temporal verification)
The current evaluator would be suitable for a simpler instruction like 'Ensure these three URLs are open in Chrome' but not for this email-based task
